items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: There are some classic Freddie Hubbard solos, some classic Clifford Brown solos,

ctx.x: I don't care what instrument you play, any instrument should learn Charlie Parker's solos. And his pieces, that's "Moose the Mooche" part of the repertoire, you've got to know and "Confirmation" and "Donna Lee," and all those -- you know, they call them "heads," I guess, the melodic -- you know, the written out part of the solo. And then you learn the ad lib solo. But I think that all instruments should learn those solos.

There are some classic Freddie Hubbard solos, some classic Clifford Brown solos, "Donna Lee," Clifford Brown solo on "Confirmation" that he made with Max Roach. That's a classic. You could spend six months on that solo, a trumpet player could, and I think any other instrument. Because I don't think that any instrument should stick to its own instrument, because each instrument's got its mechanical limitations.
